question: Does perpetual funding change the conclusion? Every earlier measurement ignored it.

funding_rates.note: A positive rate means longs pay shorts, which was the state of every instrument.

holding_period.note: The ten-bar maximum is almost never reached; a 2% stop against a 3.4% daily sigma sits inside one standard deviation.

interpretation: No. Funding was expected to be material because the policy allows a ten-bar hold, but 68.2% of episodes close in the first bar and the mean hold is 1.51 bars, so the carry never accrues. Charging only settlements strictly inside the holding interval costs 0.0064% per episode; charging full days as an upper bound costs 0.0272%. Against a measured alpha of 0.359% that is two to eight percent, and the sign of every earlier conclusion is unchanged. The finding that does matter is the holding distribution itself: the stop is inside one daily standard deviation, so most positions are resolved by noise on their first day.
limitations: Bar resolution cannot say when inside a bar a position closed, so the charged figure is a lower bound and the full-day figure an upper one.
Funding is charged at the settlement rate with no premium or cap modelling.
Short-side funding income is not modelled because no short side exists.
